description:
ABOUT THE LAND DEVELOPMENT AGENCY 

 The Land Development Agency (LDA) is a commercial, semi-State body that seeks to maximise the supply of affordable homes on public and other land in a financially sustainable manner, supporting the creation of thriving communities and delivering ongoing positive social impact. It is overseen by an independent board of directors and is funded with €5 billion of equity capital committed by the Government.

 The LDA has commenced construction on a number of projects on State land and has a delivery pipeline in excess of 17,000 homes. It also works in partnership with the country’s largest and most experienced homebuilders and will deliver a further 8,000 homes under the Government’s Project Tosaigh initiative. Additionally, the LDA is working on large-scale longer-term strategic areas by master-planning and bringing forward planning applications in locations such as Limerick Colbert Quarter, the Digital Hub in Dublin and Sandy Road in Galway.

 The Role 

 This role within an expanding Asset Management Team and will offer the right candidate a fantastic opportunity to work on a wide range of transformative projects across the country. The purpose of the role is to provide land, property and security management support, oversight and advice to internal teams within the LDA.

 The successful candidate will be an experienced property/land manager and will be tasked with management and oversight of external service providers in the delivery of land, property and security services in addition to providing advice to internal LDA Teams on asset management matters specific to land and property services.

 The ideal candidate will have all necessary technical, property/facilities and commercial acumen required to successfully oversee the management of a large portfolio of land, buildings and meanwhile uses. In addition to being a strong and effective communicator, candidates will need to be flexible, driven, motivated and critically possess the ability to be adaptable to respond to the exciting challenges of the LDA mandate. This role will afford the right candidate an opportunity to develop existing and new skills, taking their career to a new level.

 Essential duties and responsibilities: 

 Land Management 

 Oversee and proactively manage land and buildings within LDA ownership. Provide land management and support services for LDA sites and landbanks.

 Provide support to the Senior Property Manager on commercial licences and land agreements.

 Ensure land holdings are secure, safe and comply with insurance requirements.

 Engage with the LDA’s internal Insurance Team in respect of insurance requirements for all sites.

 Develop annual land management budgets, working with other LDA business units to proactively deliver value for money and suitable land management strategy.

 Deliver monthly reports on site expenditure and site performance/compliance.

 Support the Senior Property Manager in the delivery of land strategy and portfolio performance.

 Property Management 

 Day to day management of commercial property agreements and land.

 Engage appropriately with LDA approved contractors and service providers to deliver and uphold suitable repair and contractual services.

 Ensure reactive matters (repairs and otherwise) are addressed within a timely manner.

 Seek competitive quotes and instruct works in compliance with LDA public procurement guidelines.

 Oversee successful delivery of annual PPM where required.

 Undertake regular site/property inspections across Ireland.

 Engage with LDA appointed agents on land/property management matters.

 Ensure statutory compliance with applicable legislation or regulation to the sites within the allotted portfolio.

 Liaise with the LDA Finance Team to ensure efficient running of the land financial operations, including supporting the production of monthly and annual accounts, reviewing invoices for payment each month and actively investigate cost reduction opportunities.

 Monthly reporting to the Senior Property Manager in relation to the management of land, buildings and services within the allotted portfolio, including costs, operational matters and risk management.

 Support the development of LDA strategies for land and asset management.

 Collaborate with internal teams to support and implement new asset management systems to collect, store and analyse all property information for compliance and decision support purposes.

 Proactively develop skills to ensure career development. 

 Successful delivery of annual KPI’s and performance requirements.

 Other duties as may be required based on the evolving operational requirements of the LDA.

 Security Management 

 Proactive management, engagement and oversight of LDA appointed security providers.

 Complete land/site security assessments working closely with multiple LDA teams to identify security management and site handover strategy.

 Provide security and land management advice to LDA business units on a site-by-site basis.

 Deliver weekly/monthly security reports to LDA business units.

 Engage with LDA and external stakeholders on site security matters.

 Deliver annual land management and security budgets.

 Undertake regular budgetary reviews.

 Oversee, and where required complete, site security inspections of properties/land.

 Requirements: 

 Have minimum 4 years land and/or property management experience.

 Member of the SCSI or at a minimum have route to membership in progress.

 Excellent relationship management skills (both internal and external).

 Excellent communications skills – both written and verbal.

 Proficiency in MS Office, particularly Excel.

 Understanding of title and legal documents.

 Understanding of risk management and mitigation measures.

 Good knowledge and understanding of land management best practise and associated land/commercial lettings.

 Detailed knowledge of the issues and developments and current thinking in relation to best practice in Asset Management.

 Understanding of planning and development laws along with working knowledge Building Regulations and Heritage Buildings.

 Have a good working knowledge of current opportunities and trends in facilities and land management, having the capability to advise on opportunities for maximising operational efficiencies.

 Must have own car and full, clean driving license and ability to travel across Ireland.

 Additional experience and skills required: 

 Initiative-taker with the ability to prioritise.

 Solutions and results focused.

 Strong commercial awareness and sound professional judgement

 Excellent attention to detail.

 Experience of other property related IT systems desired.

 Ability to work well within a team environment.

 Flexible and adaptable. Capable of managing multiple sites via external suppliers or internal team.

 Ability to work to tight deadlines.

 To Apply: 

 The closing date for applications is 12pm on the 28th September

 The Land Development Agency is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promote and support a diverse and inclusive workforce, and we endeavour to provide reasonable accommodation as required.

ABOUT THE LAND DEVELOPMENT AGENCY 

 The Land Development Agency (LDA) is a key Government Commercial Semi-State Body that delivers social and affordable housing on State and other lands. It is overseen by an independent board of directors and the Government has committed to providing the LDA with €1.25 billion of equity which is drawn as required.

 The LDA has commenced construction on various state sourced lands and is currently working on direct delivery projects that can deliver over 5,000 homes. It is also delivering affordable housing by working with the private sector on an initiative called ‘Project Tosaigh’, which will yield a further 5,000 homes.

 Additionally, the LDA is working on large-scale longer-term strategic areas by master-planning and bringing forward planning applications in locations such as Limerick Colbert Quarter, the Digital Hub in Dublin and Sandy Road in Galway.

 Role Summary: 

 Reporting the Director of Human Resources, the Learning & Development Manager plays a key role in shaping the employee learning experience across the organisation. You will lead the Learning & Development strategy, drive capability-building initiatives, oversee onboarding and performance development processes, and partner with leaders to foster a culture of continuous learning and growth.

 This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on employee development, organisational performance, and leadership capability.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Lead the end-to-end design, development, and implementation of the organisation's annual Learning & Development Strategy, ensuring alignment with business objectives and workforce needs.

 Drive the annual Training Needs Analysis (TNA) process, partnering with people managers and leadership teams to identify learning priorities and capability gaps.

 Design, deliver, and continuously enhance internal development programmes that support employee growth, leadership capability, and career progression.

 Oversee the annual Learning & Development budget, ensuring effective planning, allocation, and monitoring of expenditure.

 Manage the internal Learning Management System (LMS) and oversee the development of a structured and engaging e-learning offer for the organisation.

 Oversee the full employee onboarding experience, ensuring a seamless and consistent integration journey for all new hires.

 Design and manage the delivery of impactful learning initiatives that strengthen employee capability, performance, and professional development across the organisation.

 Lead the delivery of the annual performance management cycle, including employee training, mid-year reviews, and year-end performance processes.

 Support the ongoing development and implementation of Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) initiatives in alignment with the organisation's EDI strategy and objectives.

 Manage and support the Learning & Development Coordinator, providing guidance, coaching, and oversight of workload planning and day-to-day activities.

 Work collaboratively with the HR team, providing support and expertise on cross-functional projects and people initiatives as required.

 Requirements 

 A bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in Learning and Development, HR Management or a related field.

 Previous experience in a similar role required.

 Proven people management experience, including leading, coaching, and developing team members

 Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.

 Ability to manage multiple projects and roll out initiatives in a timely manner.

 Ability to work on own initiative with a sound decision making ability.

 Excellent communication skills, written and oral.

 Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with staff at all levels of the organisation.

 To apply: 

 The closing date for applications is 5pm on 28th September. 

 The Land Development Agency (LDA) is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promote and support a diverse and inclusive workforce, and we endeavour to provide reasonable accommodation.

description:
ABOUT THE LAND DEVELOPMENT AGENCY 

 The Land Development Agency (LDA) is the State’s affordable housing delivery body. Its main role is to acquire and develop State and other land to deliver affordable homes, supporting the creation of thriving communities and delivering ongoing positive social impact. It is overseen by an independent Board of Directors and has total capitalisation of up to €8.75bn. description:
HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer 

We are recruiting for a number of Drainage Engineers to work in 2 person teams, covering the whole of Hampshire. This is a fantastic opportunity to start a new career with us here at Lanes Group! 

 At Lanes Group, nothing is more important than the health, safety and wellbeing of our people, our customers and the communities we serve. As one of the UK's leading infrastructure delivery partners, we employ around 5,000 talented people across a nationwide network of depots and operational locations, delivering annual revenues in excess of £650 million. 

 We provide essential infrastructure, drainage, wastewater and utility services to many of the UK's leading organisations, including a significant number of FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 companies. Our success is built on the expertise of our people, our commitment to doing things safely and professionally, and our focus on delivering outstanding service every day. 

 Strong leadership being at our heart, supporting our people ensuring they are engaged with purpose, rewarded and recognised whilst delivering absolute exacting operational excellence being a leading entity and enviable delivery team embracing quality and compliance in our overarching delivery, one of our fundamental key differentiators. 

 In this critical role of ensuring our organisation is known for being the best in everything we do, known for leaving a legacy of absolute quality and compliance and, keeping our promises at all times is our absolute mantra.

We operate 24/7 and as such you are required to work flexible hours, weekends and participate in an on-call rota. Full training / PPE / use of company equipment will be provided to ensure that all our drainage engineers have the right tools, competency, and confidence to undertake the work to Lanes’ high standard of operation regardless of background or previous experience.

 Position: HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer 

 Location: Millbrook Depot, Southampton, Hampshire 

 Job Type: Permanent, full-time 

 Hours: Monday - Friday, 50 Hours Per Week, Plus on-call rota

 Salary: OTE £50,000 per annum (made up of basic pay, overtime, on call allowance and bonuses) 

 Benefits: 21 days holiday (including bank holidays); plus your birthday off; health cash plan; onsite parking; auto enrolment pension scheme; enhanced maternity and paternity, retention loyalty scheme based on length of service, friendly working environment. 

About the role: 
Due to continued growth and development, we are now looking for customer focused people to join us in our Utility Division, working on our Southern Water contract service to deliver real and effective solutions to waste-water network and drainage problems. 

 Travelling to residential sites via a HGV in a two person team, around the region, powering a high-pressure water jet for restoration 

 Clean, clear and maintain drainage systems 

 Record each job report correctly on the specialist equipment provided 

 Run diagnostics and repairs on drains 

 Delivering good customer service 

 Maintaining good health and safety practise while carrying out works 

 Ensure vehicle stock is full and replenished 

 Comply with health and safety responsibilities, i.e. PPE / safe site setups protecting Lanes Group employees, the public and other road users 

 Utilise VISTEC and Salesforce platforms 

 Operate JHL specification vacuum tankers and associated equipment 

 Safely access vehicle cabs, sites and offices using correct procedures (e.g., three points of contact...) 

 Manipulate (including loading and unloading to / from tanker pipe storage trays) flexible pipework in a safe manner utilising correct manual handling techniques 

 Work unsupervised in all weather conditions, wearing correct PPE or utilising the lone worker system 

 Dynamically risk assess site access and working conditions depending on specific circumstances on arrival 

 Liaising with the client regarding process and any updates 

 Provide support to your colleagues 

 Conduct thorough inspections of tools, equipment and plant before and after use 

 Report any defects or malfunctions 

 Carry out risk assessments and have a mature approach to risk perception 

 Be aware of all Lanes Group policies and your responsibilities towards them 

 Any other reasonable ad-hoc tasks, duties or projects as requested by management 

 So if you enjoy working outdoors and delivering only the best in customer service, where no two days are the same and want to join a growing company that not only values you and your ability - but also strives to develop your potential and further your career progression, then we are the right Company for you. 

 What is essential is the ability to work safely to quickly diagnose and deliver practical and efficient solutions to attain the highest levels of customer satisfaction. 

 FULL TRAINING GIVEN - Great Opportunity 

 About you: 
 The ideal candidate will be hard working and respectful and comply with health and safety standards. Experience in the use of High Pressure Jetting equipment is useful but not essential. Other drainage qualifications (e.g. NRSWA and Confined Spaces) are an advantage. 

 You must have a minimum of a HGV Class 2 licence, completed he certificate of professional competence (CPC), and have an up to date digi tachograph card. 

 At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. We believe that our differences make us stronger and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented groups. Join us in our commitment to creating a more inclusive and diverse world. 

 Lanes Group are a signatory of the ‘Charter for Employer Positive About Mental Health’ run by Mindful Em ployer.

 Strong leadership being at our heart, supporting our people ensuring they are engaged with purpose, rewarded and recognised whilst delivering absolute exacting operational excellence being a leading entity and enviable delivery team embracing quality and compliance in our overarching delivery, one of our fundamental key differentiators. 

 In this critical role of ensuring our organisation is known for being the best in everything we do, known for leaving a legacy of absolute quality and compliance and, keeping our promises at all times is our absolute mantra.

 Location: Durrington Head Office, Worthing, West Sussex 

 Job Type: Permanent, full-time 

 Hours: 4 nights on 4 nights off, 38.5 hours per week, (7:30pm - 7:30am). 

 Salary: £28 ,890 per annum, depending upon experience 

 Benefits: 23 days holiday (including bank holidays); plus your birthday off; onsite restaurant; onsite parking; personal learning; health cash plan; auto enrolment pension scheme; enhanced maternity and paternity, friendly working environment.

 Undertake any other work as reasonably required of you by the Customer Operations Manager or Senior Scheduler. 

 Work closely with Field Management teams to maximise resources and ensure customer issues are resolved as timely as possible and to an industry leading standard. 

 Be part of high performing teams that embrace a culture of continuous improvement, delivering process change and operational efficiencies. 

 Establish positive and productive client relationships, ensuring regular, constructive two-way communication. 

 Ensure all resources are utilised effectively - maximising output whilst minimising cost. 

 Act as a customer champion supporting the design and implementation of customer experience initiatives and protecting Lanes Group brand and reputation and safeguarding against future claims and disputes. 

 Anticipate future operational or compliance risks, mitigating or escalating as required. 

 Ensure end to end process compliance, identifying and removing blockers and ineffective ways of working. 

 Be aware of all Lanes Group policies and your responsibilities towards them. 

 Any reasonable ad-hoc tasks, duties or projects requested by management.

 Be hard working and respectful 

 Comply with health and safety standards.

 Be resourceful and proactive 

 Multi-task, prioritise, work under pressure and on own initiative 

 Have the ability to deal with people at different levels 

 At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. job_title: HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer - Patching and Lining
description:
Patching and Lining HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer 

We are thrilled to announce a major contract win with Southern Water! We are recruiting for a number of Drainage Engineers to work in 2 person teams, covering the whole of Kent on our Patching and Lining team. This is a fantastic opportunity to start a new career with us here at Lanes Group! 

 At Lanes Group nothing is more important than the health, safety and well-being of our people and our customers. It’s a major reason we are the UK’s largest independent specialist infrastructure delivery partner of choice with a turnover in excess of £530 million, (EBITDA £45m), with over 4,000 brilliant people and a countrywide network of operational locations. Our services cover the majority of the FTSE 100 & 250 respectfully. 

 Strong leadership being at our heart, supporting our people ensuring they are engaged with purpose, rewarded and recognised whilst delivering absolute exacting operational excellence being a leading entity and enviable delivery team embracing quality and compliance in our overarching delivery, one of our fundamental key differentiators. 

 In this critical role of ensuring our organisation is known for being the best in everything we do, known for leaving a legacy of absolute quality and compliance and, keeping our promises at all times is our absolute mantra.

We operate 24/7 and as such you are required to work flexible hours, weekends and participate in an on-call rota. Full training / PPE / use of company equipment will be provided to ensure that all our drainage engineers have the right tools, competency, and confidence to undertake the work to Lanes’ high standard of operation regardless of background or previous experience.

 Position: HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer - Patching and Lining 

 Location: Crawley Depot, West Sussex 

 Job Type: Permanent, full-time 

 Hours: Monday to Friday, 50 hours per week

 Salary: OTE £50,000 per annum (made up of basic pay, overtime, on call allowance and bonuses) 

 Benefits: 21 days holiday (plus bank holidays); health cash plan; onsite parking; auto enrolment pension scheme; friendly working environment. 

About the role: 
Due to continued growth and development, we are now looking for customer focused people to join us in our Utility Division, working on our Southern Water contract service to deliver real and effective solutions to waste-water network and drainage problems.

 Travelling to residential sites via a specially equipped van in a two person team, around the region. 

 Repair and maintain drainage systems, installing patch liners to carry out first-time-fix sewer and drain repair. 

 Utilise the Picote system to remove scale, roots, concrete, and other hard obstructions that high pressure water jetting systems can’t remove. 

 Survey the network of drainage systems and assess pip conditions to produce high quality reports with the help of state of the art drain surveying equipment. 

 Record each job report correctly on the specialist equipment provided. 

 Delivering good customer service. 

 Maintaining good H&S practise while carrying out works. 

 Ensure vehicle stock is full and replenished. 

 To comply with health and safety responsibilities i.e. PPE / safe site set ups protecting Lanes Group employees, the public and other road users. 

 To be able to utilise VISTEC and Salesforce platforms. 

 Liaising with the client regarding progress and any updates. 

 Ability to work unsupervised in all weather conditions utilising correct PPE, lone worker system, etc. 

 Dynamically risk assess site access & working conditions depending on specific circumstances on arrival. 

 Provide support to your colleagues. 

 To conduct thorough inspections of tools, equipment and plant before/after use. 

 Report any defects or malfunctions in regards to training. 

 Carry out risk assessments and have a mature approach to risk perception. 

 Be aware of all Lanes Group policies and your responsibility towards them. 

 Any other reasonable ad-hoc duties requested by management . 

So if you enjoy working outdoors and delivering only the best in customer service, where no two days are the same and want to join a growing company that not only values you and your ability - but also strives to develop your potential and further your career progression, then we are the right Company for you. 

 What is essential is the ability to work safely to quickly diagnose and deliver practical and efficient solutions to attain the highest levels of customer satisfaction. 

 About you: 
 The ideal candidate will be hard working and respectful and comply with health and safety standards. Experience in the use of High Pressure Jetting equipment is useful but not essential, as is Confined Space Entry training (AP2). Other drainage qualifications (e.g. NRSWA and OS19X) are an advantage. 

 Due to the weight of the specialised van (5.5T), you must have a minimum of a HGV Class 2 licence, completed the certificate of professional competence (CPC), and have an up to date digi tachograph card. 

 At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. We believe that our differences make us stronger and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented groups. Join us in our commitment to creating a more inclusive and diverse world. 

 Lanes Group are a signatory of the ‘Charter for Employer Positive About Mental Health’ run by Mindful Em ployer.

description:
Patching and Lining HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer 

We are thrilled to announce a major contract win with Southern Water! We are recruiting for a number of Drainage Engineers to work in 2 person teams, covering the whole of Kent on our Patching and Lining team. This is a fantastic opportunity to start a new career with us here at Lanes Group! 

 At Lanes Group nothing is more important than the health, safety and well-being of our people and our customers. It’s a major reason we are the UK’s largest independent specialist infrastructure delivery partner of choice with a turnover in excess of £530 million, (EBITDA £45m), with over 4,000 brilliant people and a countrywide network of operational locations. Our services cover the majority of the FTSE 100 & 250 respectfully. 

 Strong leadership being at our heart, supporting our people ensuring they are engaged with purpose, rewarded and recognised whilst delivering absolute exacting operational excellence being a leading entity and enviable delivery team embracing quality and compliance in our overarching delivery, one of our fundamental key differentiators. 

 In this critical role of ensuring our organisation is known for being the best in everything we do, known for leaving a legacy of absolute quality and compliance and, keeping our promises at all times is our absolute mantra.

We operate 24/7 and as such you are required to work flexible hours, weekends and participate in an on-call rota. Full training / PPE / use of company equipment will be provided to ensure that all our drainage engineers have the right tools, competency, and confidence to undertake the work to Lanes’ high standard of operation regardless of background or previous experience.

 Position: HGV Class 2 Drainage Engineer - Patching and Lining 

 Location: Crawley Depot, West Sussex 

 Job Type: Permanent, full-time 

 Hours: Monday to Friday, 50 hours per week

 Salary: OTE £50,000 per annum (made up of basic pay, overtime, on call allowance and bonuses) 

 Benefits: 21 days holiday (plus bank holidays); health cash plan; onsite parking; auto enrolment pension scheme; friendly working environment. 

About the role: 
Due to continued growth and development, we are now looking for customer focused people to join us in our Utility Division, working on our Southern Water contract service to deliver real and effective solutions to waste-water network and drainage problems.

 Travelling to residential sites via a specially equipped van in a two person team, around the region. 

 Repair and maintain drainage systems, installing patch liners to carry out first-time-fix sewer and drain repair. 

 Utilise the Picote system to remove scale, roots, concrete, and other hard obstructions that high pressure water jetting systems can’t remove. 

 Survey the network of drainage systems and assess pip conditions to produce high quality reports with the help of state of the art drain surveying equipment. 

 Record each job report correctly on the specialist equipment provided. 

 Delivering good customer service. 

 Maintaining good H&S practise while carrying out works. 

 Ensure vehicle stock is full and replenished. 

 To comply with health and safety responsibilities i.e. PPE / safe site set ups protecting Lanes Group employees, the public and other road users. 

 To be able to utilise VISTEC and Salesforce platforms. 

 Liaising with the client regarding progress and any updates. 

 Ability to work unsupervised in all weather conditions utilising correct PPE, lone worker system, etc. 

 Dynamically risk assess site access & working conditions depending on specific circumstances on arrival. 

 Provide support to your colleagues. 

 To conduct thorough inspections of tools, equipment and plant before/after use. 

 Report any defects or malfunctions in regards to training. 

 Carry out risk assessments and have a mature approach to risk perception. 

 Be aware of all Lanes Group policies and your responsibility towards them. 

 Any other reasonable ad-hoc duties requested by management . 

So if you enjoy working outdoors and delivering only the best in customer service, where no two days are the same and want to join a growing company that not only values you and your ability - but also strives to develop your potential and further your career progression, then we are the right Company for you. 

 What is essential is the ability to work safely to quickly diagnose and deliver practical and efficient solutions to attain the highest levels of customer satisfaction. 

 About you: 
 The ideal candidate will be hard working and respectful and comply with health and safety standards. Experience in the use of High Pressure Jetting equipment is useful but not essential, as is Confined Space Entry training (AP2). Other drainage qualifications (e.g. NRSWA and OS19X) are an advantage. 

 Due to the weight of the specialised van (5.5T), you must have a minimum of a HGV Class 2 licence, completed the certificate of professional competence (CPC), and have an up to date digi tachograph card. 

 At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. We believe that our differences make us stronger and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented groups. Join us in our commitment to creating a more inclusive and diverse world. 

 Lanes Group are a signatory of the ‘Charter for Employer Positive About Mental Health’ run by Mindful Em ployer.

description:
Established in 2013, Sapphire Utility Solutions has quickly become the partner of choice for many clients across the UK in our chosen markets. 

 We provide award winning services to the clean water, wastewater, gas, multi utilities and the highways sector. We are passionate about working alongside our client’s and partners to maintain the utility services essential to modern life throughout the UK.

 Make a difference every day 

 50 hours per week 

 Hourly rate - £43,498 per annum

 Rotating shifts: Monday–Sunday

 Do you enjoy solving problems, helping people and working in a role where every day brings something different?

 Join our team as a Solo Solver and play an important part in protecting our customers, communities and the environment.

 About the role 

 As a Solo Solver, you’ll be one of the first points of contact when wastewater incidents or customer issues arise.

 You’ll investigate problems, identify what has caused them and make sure the appropriate action is taken. You’ll also help ensure customers receive a professional and efficient service throughout the process.

 The role is practical and varied, with much of the work carried out independently as a “Solo Solver”. You could be responding to blockages, odours or pest incidents, carrying out investigations and inspections, and taking ownership of resolving issues safely and effectively, while liaising with specialist teams where more complex support is required.

 What you’ll be doing 

 Respond to wastewater incidents, including flooding, blockages, Pest and equipment problems.

 Investigate issues and identify their underlying causes.

 Carry out practical work such as high-pressure water jetting and CCTV surveys where required.

 Communicate with customers and provide clear updates throughout an incident.

 Work closely with colleagues, contractors and external partners to resolve problems efficiently.

 Follow all health and safety requirements and environmental procedures.

 Record incident information accurately and complete relevant reports.

 Issue appropriate notices when access to private property is required for essential work.

 Keep customers informed from the beginning of an incident through to completion.

 Make sure jobs are properly closed down and record any lessons that could improve future responses.

 Assist with local incident response when larger or more serious events occur.

 Help with customer-awareness campaigns and provide advice on issues such as appropriate items to dispose of or flush.

 What we’re looking for 

 To be successful in this role, you’ll ideally have: 

 5 GCSEs (A–C) or equivalent, including Maths and English.

 A full UK driving licence.

 The ability and willingness to work in confined spaces.

 An understanding of water industry standards and regulatory requirements.

 Good communication and interpersonal skills.

 The ability to work alone effectively along with different teams and departments when necessary.

 Strong organisation and time-management skills.

 A practical approach to investigating and resolving problems.

 The ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with pressure or difficult situations.

 Good written communication skills and the ability to produce clear and accurate reports.

 A willingness to work independently while also contributing positively as part of a team.

 Working hours 

 The position is based on a 48 hour working week with a rotating shift arrangement.

 You will work 12-hour shifts, with operational coverage between 08:00 and 20:00, Monday to Sunday.

 Weekend working will therefore form part of the normal rota.

 You’ll enjoy this role if you… 

 * Like helping people and making a difference when situations are difficult.

 * Are confident speaking to customers face-to-face and over the telephone.

 * Can explain information clearly and in a straightforward way.

 * Enjoy practical, hands-on work and finding solutions to problems.

 * Can work confidently on your own while also contributing to a wider team.

 * Are dependable, organised and able to adapt when priorities change.

 * Enjoy a varied working environment where no two days are necessarily the same.

 What you can expect 

 This is a varied role where your work can have a direct impact on customers, local communities and the environment.

 You’ll have the opportunity to develop your practical and technical skills while working alongside an experienced team. Training and ongoing development will support you in building your knowledge and progressing within the role.

 If you’re someone who takes pride in helping people, solving problems and doing a job properly, we’d love to hear from you.

The position is based on a 48 hour working week with a rotating shift arrangement.

 

You will work 12-hour shifts, with operational coverage between 08:00 and 20:00, Monday to Sunday.

 

Weekend working will therefore form part of the normal rota.

 

You’ll enjoy this role if you…

 

* Like helping people and making a difference when situations are difficult.

* Are confident speaking to customers face-to-face and over the telephone.

* Can explain information clearly and in a straightforward way.

* Enjoy practical, hands-on work and finding solutions to problems.

* Can work confidently on your own while also contributing to a wider team.

* Are dependable, organised and able to adapt when priorities change.

* Enjoy a varied working environment where no two days are necessarily the same.

 

What you can expect

 

This is a varied role where your work can have a direct impact on customers, local communities and the environment.

 

You’ll have the opportunity to develop your practical and technical skills while working alongside an experienced team. Training and ongoing development will support you in building your knowledge and progressing within the role.

 

If you’re someone who takes pride in helping people, solving problems and doing a job properly, we’d love to hear from you.

Planning Coordinator 

 We are thrilled to announce a major contract win with Southern Water! We are recruiting for a Planning Coordinator to manage and plan jobs for our civils engineers in our Special Projects Division. This is a fantastic opportunity to grow your career with us here at Lanes Group! 

 At Lanes Group nothing is more important than the health, safety and well-being of our people and our customers. It’s a major reason we are the UK’s largest independent specialist infrastructure delivery partner of choice with a turnover in excess of £530 million, (EBITDA £45m), with over 4,000 brilliant people and a countrywide network of operational locations. Our services cover the majority of the FTSE 100 & 250 respectfully. 

 Strong leadership being at our heart, supporting our people ensuring they are engaged with purpose, rewarded and recognised whilst delivering absolute exacting operational excellence being a leading entity and enviable delivery team embracing quality and compliance in our overarching delivery, one of our fundamental key differentiators. 

 In this critical role of ensuring our organisation is known for being the best in everything we do, known for leaving a legacy of absolute quality and compliance and, keeping our promises at all times is our absolute mantra. 

 Position: Planning Coordinator (may also be known in the industry as Flow Control Coordinator) 

 Location: Durrington West Sussex 

 Job Type: permanent, full time 

 Hours: Monday to Friday, 40 hours 

 Salary: £27,000 to £29,000 - depending upon experience 

 Benefits: 24 days holiday (plus bank holidays); plus your birthday off; health cash plan; onsite parking; auto enrolment pension scheme; enhanced maternity and paternity, friendly working environment. 

 About the role: 

 Planning is central to maintaining workflow accuracy and timely job completion, acting as a liaison between contractors, internal teams, and customers. The Planning Coordinator plays a vital role in daily job dispatch, communication, and reporting to support operational excellence across Lanes Group service areas, ensuring the efficient coordination, processing, scheduling, and closure of jobs. 

 Job Management & Scheduling 

 Assess the Big Change system daily for new job requests. 

 Allocate and dispatch jobs to the appropriate crews based on scope, location, and availability. 

 Schedule jobs (P1/2/2a/3), ensuring timely follow-up. 

 Liaise with internal contacts and third-parties to identify responsible units 

 Update contractor assignments in Big Change and notify external teams where applicable. 

 Plan jobs for crews daily and book appointments directly with customers via calls or texts. 

 Maintain clear and professional communication with customers to confirm appointment scheduling. 

 Coordinate with other units when joint efforts are needed to complete job activities within boundary areas. 

 Job Closure & Reporting 

 Monitor the email inboxes for communication, inquiry and reports. 

 Close down jobs via Big change. 

 Escalate unresolved job backlogs to relevant managers. 

 Raise follow-on works in Ellipse where further job actions are required. 

 Update job details in Big Change as needed based on new information or feedback. 

 Inbox & Communication Management 

 Manage multiple shared inboxes, ensuring timely responses and clean inboxes daily. 

 Handle all customer and contractor enquiries promptly, flagging follow-ups as "awaiting response" where needed. 

 System & Spreadsheet Maintenance 

 Update and maintain the Whereabout spreadsheet, closing jobs marked in green and deleting lines once jobs are completed. 

 Ensure all record-keeping across systems (e.g., BIG CHANGE, Waterworx, Whereabout spreadsheet) is current and accurate. 

 Update the whereabouts sheet to reflect operative locations and availability. 

 Team Collaboration & Support 

 Liaise with other operatives to ensure job completion and resolve logistical challenges.

 Collaborate with other business units and field teams for support and coordination on joint activities. 

 Report regularly to the Operations Manager with updates and progress on scheduling, job status, and support needs. 

 Be aware of all Lanes Group policies and your responsibilities towards them. 

 Any other reasonable ad-hoc tasks, duties and projects requested by management. 

 So if you enjoy working in a fast paced environment and delivering only the best in customer service, where no two days are the same and want to join a growing company that not only values you and your ability - but also strives to develop your potential and further your career progression, then we are the right Company for you. 

 What is essential is the ability to work safely to quickly diagnose and deliver practical and efficient solutions to attain the highest levels of customer satisfaction. 

 About you: 

 The ideal candidate will: 

 Be hard working and respectful 

 Comply with health and safety standards. 

 Have great interpersonal skills to create relationships with the team, engineers, and wider Lanes Group network 

 Have good knowledge of Microsoft 365 

 Be proficient in job management platforms (e.g Big Change, Waterworx, Ellipse) 

 Have solid communication skills (both written and verbal) with professional telephone and email etiquette 

 Be resourceful and proactive 

 Multi-task, prioritise, work under pressure and on own initiative 

 Have the ability to deal with people at different levels 

 At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. We believe that our differences make us stronger and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented groups. Join us in our commitment to creating a more inclusive and diverse world. 

 Lanes Group are a signatory of the 'Charter for Employer Positive About Mental Health' run by Mindful Employer.
